newsitem.title: CHINA: China rebel rocker's song in literary compilation.
newsitem.headline: China rebel rocker's song in literary compilation.

text.p: China's most famous rock and roll star, Cui Jian, who was at one point banned from performing in public, has joined the ranks of the country's literary luminaries, Shanghai's Xinmin Evening News said on Wednesday.

Lyrics of Cui's song "Nothing To My Name," which became an anthem for student demonstrators during the pro-democracy movement of 1989, have been included in a new literary compendium published by Beijing University, it said.
The song, which remained a rallying cry for disillusioned youth long after the movement was crushed, has been published in "A Hundred Years of Chinese Literature," the newspaper said.

Following the Communist Party's June 4 crackdown on the demonstrations in Tiananmen Square, which ended when the army was sent into central Beijing, Cui and other young musicians were for months banned from performing publicly.
Regarded as the elder statesman of Chinese rock and roll, Cui has in recent years largely taken a back seat to younger performers.
